violations.description: The otherwise-valid expired/future proof fixture derives issuance and five-minute expiry from live Node Date.now(), then submits the HMAC proof to a real database clock. No fake or injected clock governs this fixture; proof validity depends on the relation between the runner clock, DB clock and elapsed scheduling time. This meets H2 even though the offsets provide a useful practical margin.

violations.description: The synthetic proof gets only three seconds remaining from live PostgreSQL clock_timestamp(), before asynchronous contact-lock acquisition, second-session startup and pg_blocking_pids polling. Later observed-expiry polling proves a real post-lock boundary, but does not freeze or remove this live-clock freshness race.
